title: Lexical entry
description: A dictionary entry: a headword with one or more senses and translations. Content record — carries full governance metadata.

partOfSpeech.description: Stable word-class id. This list is the contract half of PARTS_OF_SPEECH in services/functions/src/lexical-kinds.ts and kPartsOfSpeech in apps/mobile/lib/features/contribute/words/data/parts_of_speech.dart; all three must agree. It is long on purpose: a six-item dropdown describes a form, not a language, and everything it cannot name lands in "other", which is where data goes to stop being searchable. Kasem is a Gur language with a large productive ideophone class, and a bound morpheme is a real lexical entry that is not a noun.

nounClass.description: The noun class this entry belongs to, or null when it has not been established. Null rather than a guess: an unrecognised definite ending means the class inventory has not yet been attested, and a plausible-looking invented class is worse for the language record than an admitted gap.

forms.description:
Morphological forms that cannot be derived from the headword.

The indefinite is deliberately absent. In Kasem it is invariantly the noun followed by the particle `mo`, which makes it a rule rather than per-entry data; storing it on every row would denormalise a fact about the language into thousands of copies that all become wrong the day the rule is refined. It is derived on read by indefiniteForm() in services/functions/src/kasem-morphology.ts.

The definite is here because it is the one form that genuinely varies: it changes with the noun class, and it is what nounClass is induced from.
